userStories.title: Validate access-token sessions and revoke only the current session on logout
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enforce session activity for access JWTs and make logout transactional and scoped to the current device, with a legacy tokenVersion fallback.

**Motivation** — `AuthService.logout` bumps `User.tokenVersion`, which revokes all of the user's sessions on every device.

**Approach** — **Session check on access tokens.** `JwtAuthProvider.getPrincipal` copies `sid` onto the principal as `sessionId` (`sid` joins the claim allow-list in its SECURITY note). When `sid` is present, the principal is `revoked` if the session is not active. The answer comes from `AuthSessionService.isActive(sid, now)` and is cached 60 seconds as the object `{ active: boolean }`; an object, not a bare boolean, so a cached `false` is never read as a miss. The cache key is `authSessionCacheKey(sid)`, a new helper in `token-version.cache.ts` returning `['auth-session', sid]`. Every revoke in this feature evicts that key by direct key. Tag eviction is not enough, because the MEMORY cache strategy has no tag registry (see the note in `AuthService.logout`).

**Legacy tokens.** A refresh token without a `sid` or `jti` claim (issued before this feature) is refused with 401 before any write, so every user logs in once after the deploy. An access token without `sid` stays valid until it expires (15 minutes) and is checked by `tokenVersion` only, as today. The refresh refusal belongs to US-004; preserve only the legacy access behavior here.

**Logout.** `AuthService.logout(userId, sessionId?)`:
- **With a `sessionId`:** runs `AuthSessionService.revoke(sessionId, userId, 'logout', now)` inside the existing `this.audit.audited(...)` call, so the revoke and the `session.logout` entry commit or roll back together. The entry is recorded whether `revoke` returned true or false (logging out an already-ended session answers 200). It then evicts `authSessionCacheKey(sessionId)`. `tokenVersion` is not bumped.
- **Without a `sessionId`** (a legacy access token, or an agent principal): bumps `tokenVersion` and evicts the user's caches, exactly as today.

The logout route's `@ApiOperation` summary becomes "Revoke the current session (all sessions for a token issued before sessions)"; after that change run `bun run generate` from the repo root so `openapi.json` and the CLI client stay current. `AuthController.logout` types its principal as `KodaPrincipal` (per `.nax/rules/api-core.md`) and calls `authService.logout(user.id, isUserPrincipal(user) ? user.sessionId : undefined)`.

**Unchanged all-session levers.** Admin disable and Owner binding changes still bump `tokenVersion`, and the refresh strategy and `UserAuthState` still refuse on it, so those levers still end every session.

`revoke` has no bookkeeping wrapper; its caller records an entry in the same transaction. Implement owner-checked conditional revocation only if not already revoked, and isActive as an existence/read check for not revoked and expiresAt > now. These extend the US-001 service and private repository; no Prisma call belongs in JwtAuthProvider or AuthService. For a logout naming another user's session, nothing is revoked, tokenVersion is not bumped and session.logout is still recorded. If the session.logout audit entry fails, the session revoke rolls back with it. Preserve the existing entry { key: 'session.logout', resourceType: 'user', resourceId: userId, projectId: null, summary: 'logged out' }.

**Scope** — In: service/repository revoke and isActive, direct session cache-key helper, cached access activity check, UserPrincipal.sessionId, controller forwarding and session-scoped audited logout, plus required OpenAPI/CLI artifact regeneration. Out: new-session JWT issuance (US-002), refresh rotation orchestration and reuse audit/eviction (US-004), invite mail deferral (US-005). A "log out of all devices" control and a list of active sessions per user; logout revokes the current session only. Self-service password change and password reset; they are the follow-up feature `auth-passwords`, which adds `AuthSessionService.revokeAllForUser` on top of this feature's store. The web `/api/auth/me` outage handling (review D/BUG-6 residual) and the expired-cookie e2e; they are a separate bundle. No handwritten CLI authentication behavior changes are included; the required generated logout-summary update remains in scope. Keep workdir apps/api per the binding structure; generation is run at the root and may update existing generated root/CLI files.

**Interface** —

```typescript
/** Revokes one session if it belongs to userId and is not yet revoked; false otherwise. */
revoke(sessionId: string, userId: string, reason: SessionRevokeReason, now: Date): Promise<boolean>;
isActive(sessionId: string, now: Date): Promise<boolean>;
```

`UserPrincipal` (`auth/principal/koda-principal.types.ts`): Target adds `readonly sessionId?: string`.

`AuthService.logout` target: `logout(userId: string, sessionId?: string)`.

`AuthController.logout` target: `logout(@Principal() user: KodaPrincipal)` calling `authService.logout(user.id, isUserPrincipal(user) ? user.sessionId : undefined)`.

Update jwt-auth.provider.spec.ts with an AuthSessionService mock, allowed sid propagation and a cache that distinguishes user/session keys and retains { active: false }. Update auth.controller.spec.ts logout forwarding expectations and auth.service.spec.ts logout cases while retaining legacy version bump and user-cache eviction cases. Adapt test/integration/audit/audit-logout.integration.spec.ts so audit failure during a session-carrying logout asserts revokedAt stays null and HTTP 500, keeping its successful session.logout entry assertion. Add warm-cache/two-device and foreign-owner integration cases in test/integration/auth/session-logout.integration.spec.ts. Use real PostgreSQL and application boot for DI and rollback behavior; preserve the no-DB module compilation test from US-002. Never hand-edit openapi.json or apps/cli/src/generated/sdk.gen.ts.

AC-5 [integration] After that reuse, an AuditEntry exists with key session.refresh, resourceType 'user', resourceId the user's id, projectId null and summary 'refresh token reuse; session revoked'.
AC-6 [integration] After that reuse, POST /api/auth/refresh with the newest refresh token of the same session answers 401.

AC-12 [integration] After POST /api/auth/logout with a session's access token, POST /api/auth/refresh with that session's newest refresh token answers 401.

AC-13 [unit] When rotate returns { kind: 'reused', userId } and the audit write rejects, AuthService.refresh rejects with AuthException (401), not the audit error, and logs the audit failure with Logger.warn.
AC-14 [integration; failure handling] When a correctly signed refresh JWT names an expired or unknown AuthSession, POST /api/auth/refresh answers 401 auth and records no session.refresh AuditEntry.

AC-15 [integration; failure handling] When a correctly signed refresh JWT names an unknown jti for a live session (with GET /api/auth/me first answered 200 for that session's access token), POST /api/auth/refresh answers 401, the session's revokedReason is 'reuse', and the same GET /api/auth/me then answers 401.

routing.reasoning: Refresh composes the already-built rotation store with direct cache invalidation and a separate audited transaction, including failure isolation and concurrent HTTP lifecycles; JWT/session security mandates strict three-session TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the `refresh` cases expect a new pair from any non-revoked principal via `issueSession`; refresh now requires `extra.sessionId`/`extra.tokenId` and goes through `AuthSessionService.rotate`, so the cases gain a `rotate` mock per outcome.

the endpoint e2e rule requires the reuse-after-grace 401 case for the refresh route here, and the comment before the post-logout refresh ("signed with a stale tokenVersion") is rewritten: the refusal now comes from the revoked session.

outOfScope: expiry of the refresh JWT itself is enforced by `JwtRefreshGuard`'s signature and `exp` check, which this story does not change; disabled users and `tokenVersion` bumps keep refusing through `KodaJwtRefreshStrategyProvider`'s existing check.

userStories.title: Send approved invite emails only after transaction commit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Defer new-address invite and resend email delivery until an owning approval transaction commits while preserving immediate-route emailed results.

**Motivation** — A rollback leaves a sent link for an invite that was never stored, and a retry sends a second email.

**Approach** — In `ProjectInvitesService` (`apps/api/src/projects/invites/project-invites.service.ts`), `create` (its new-address path, `inviteNewAddress`) and `resend` hand the email send to `AfterCommitService.defer`. This mirrors `TicketTransitionsService`: `if (!this.afterCommit.defer(task)) await task()`. `AfterCommitService` is exported by `PermissionsModule`, and the constructor gains `private readonly afterCommit: AfterCommitService` as its last parameter.

- **`defer` returns true:** an approval execution owns the transaction (`ApprovalExecutionService` wraps it in `afterCommit.scope`). The send runs after that transaction commits, a rollback drops it, and the result reports `emailed: false`.
- **`defer` returns false:** the immediate route path, where `ApprovalGateService.gate` calls `command.execute` with no scope open. The send is awaited inline as today, and `emailed` reports its outcome.

Use the existing sendInvite wrapper and email.configured gate for both create's new-address path and resend. Initialize emailed to false and wrap the boolean send in a Promise<void> task compatible with AfterCommitService; the fallback awaits it and returns its outcome, while deferred approval results stay false. Do not change the existing-user direct membership path or its MEMBER_ADDED scheduling. Inject the existing global PermissionsModule AfterCommitService instance rather than constructing another instance in production: ApprovalExecutionService already opens the owning scope. No change to ApprovalExecutionService's transaction ownership is needed. A rollback never invokes the deferred mail task. Preserve sendInvite's warn-and-return-false failure behavior and InviteMailer's one INVITE schedule, immediate dispatcher send and raw-token-only-in-memory contract.

**Scope** — In: append AfterCommitService to the ProjectInvitesService constructor, defer new-address invite/resend sends, preserve immediate outcomes and pin real approved-agent result/delivery behavior. Out: session store/issuance/access/logout/refresh work (US-001 through US-004), password workflows, changes to invite acceptance, and a durable email retry/outbox redesign. Changing the `emailed` field's API description or the web invite panel's `notEmailed` copy; an approved (deferred) invite now reports `emailed: false` and the panel shows its not-emailed text, while the email itself goes out after commit.

**Interface** — Constructor addition: `private readonly afterCommit: AfterCommitService`. Existing consumed contracts: `AfterCommitService.scope(fn)` and `defer(task): boolean`; `InviteMailer.sendInvite(input): Promise<boolean>`. Mirror `if (!this.afterCommit.defer(task)) await task()`. The task uses the existing `AfterCommitTask = () => Promise<void>` contract and does not expose token material in stored results, audit payloads or logs.

Update apps/api/src/projects/invites/project-invites.service.spec.ts so its direct constructor gains a real `new AfterCommitService()` as the last argument; retain immediate-path emailed expectations and test scope callback ordering, exactly-once flush, callback-throw rollback, deferred emailed:false, and resend ordering. Add test/integration/projects/invite-after-commit.integration.spec.ts using the existing email-on fixture pattern from test/integration/email/email-dispatcher.integration.spec.ts: set SMTP_URL before boot, stub NOTIFY_SERVICE.send to resolve, create an agent invite held for approval, and approve via POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions with { "decision": "approve" }. Assert the stored approval result is emailed:false and exactly one INVITE EmailSchedule is SENT after the decision returns. Keep the real application transaction, permission bindings and audit/write guards so the integration exercises ApprovalExecutionService.scope rather than merely a mailer mock.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] ProjectInvitesService.create for a new address, called inside AfterCommitService.scope, does not call InviteMailer.sendInvite before the scope's callback resolves.
AC-2 [unit] After that scope's callback resolves, InviteMailer.sendInvite has been called exactly once.
AC-3 [unit] When the callback passed to AfterCommitService.scope throws after ProjectInvitesService.create ran, InviteMailer.sendInvite is never called.
AC-4 [unit] ProjectInvitesService.create inside a scope returns emailed: false.
AC-5 [unit] ProjectInvitesService.create outside any scope, with email configured and InviteMailer.sendInvite resolving true, returns emailed: true.
AC-6 [unit] ProjectInvitesService.resend inside a scope calls InviteMailer.sendInvite only after the scope's callback resolves.

AC-7 [integration] With SMTP_URL set before boot and NOTIFY_SERVICE.send stubbed to resolve, an agent's invite create held for approval and approved through POST /api/approvals/:id/decisions with { "decision": "approve" } stores an approval result with emailed: false.
AC-8 [integration] In that same flow, exactly one EmailSchedule row with kind 'INVITE' and status 'SENT' exists for the new invite after the decision returns.

routing.reasoning: A localized existing after-commit pattern changes two mail-send paths and constructor fixtures; strict security TDD applies because invite credential delivery crosses approval transaction boundaries.

modifiedFiles.reason: the service is constructed with its current dependencies; it gains the `AfterCommitService` argument (a real `new AfterCommitService()`), and the existing `emailed` expectations on the immediate path stay.

analysis:
Repository verification and architecture
This is an enhancement to an existing NestJS 12/Fastify API, not greenfield. The codebase-memory MCP server/tools were unavailable in this session, so discovery used direct repository reads and text searches rooted at /Users/williamkhoo/workspace/subrina-coder/projects/koda/repos/koda. No executable shell was available; this PRD is based on source inspection, not a claimed test run. Read .nax/mono/apps/api/context.md before implementation and follow .nax/rules/api-core.md:12-22 and api-data.md:26-97. The nathapp-nestjs-patterns skill was not found in repository files; implementers must read it if their host exposes it. The API owns business logic, persistence and auth; no web, runner or handwritten CLI behavior changes are needed. The supplied automatic web stack label is stale: repository guidance and the auth cookie extractor identify a Nuxt SSR client, not Next.js (apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts:35-41). The installed Nathapp dependencies are ~4.2.4 (apps/api/package.json:47-61), despite older v3/4.1 references in context; use the installed interfaces and established Nathapp patterns, not a package downgrade or a replacement auth stack.

Current authentication and callers
AuthService currently signs stateless pairs: JwtPayload lacks sid (apps/api/src/auth/auth.service.ts:21-26), register calls issueSession after its membership/user/audit transaction commits (auth.service.ts:84-116), login checks password and disabled state then calls issueSession (auth.service.ts:124-142), refresh checks principal.revoked and a fresh missing/disabled-user lookup then calls issueSession (auth.service.ts:145-158). issueSession derives the binding-based role once and constructs AuthResponseDto without persistence (auth.service.ts:170-180); token generators currently accept four and two arguments respectively (auth.service.ts:206-213). InviteAcceptanceService is the third session-starting flow and already calls auth.issueSession only after its account/invite/binding transaction commits (apps/api/src/projects/invites/invite-acceptance.service.ts:65-109). Keep those transaction boundaries and the response shape; role is a compatibility/display claim, not an authorization source. Local IPrincipal already allows extra?: Record<string, unknown> (apps/api/src/auth/types.ts:1-8), so refresh can carry sessionId and tokenId without inventing another principal contract.

Storage and migration
User currently has tokenVersion, disabled and its other relations but no authSessions relation (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:25-42); there are no files under src/auth/sessions today. US-001 creates AuthSession and RefreshToken, the named migration 20261210090000_auth_sessions/migration.sql, a domain/token file, a private AbstractPrismaRepository implementation, a leaf module and a service. Add exactly the specified indexes, cascades, nullability and service-generated UUID primary keys, retaining User.tokenVersion. No backfill is required or specified: predeploy refresh JWTs are deliberately rejected after US-004, while predeploy access JWTs remain tokenVersion-only for their remaining 15-minute lifetime. Apply the additive PostgreSQL migration and regenerate the gitignored Prisma client before using the new delegates; do not manually edit generated Prisma output. The schema generator uses prisma-client output ../src/generated/prisma with CommonJS (schema.prisma:4-8); generated client imports, not @prisma/client imports, belong in repository/persistence mapping code. Test DBs are rebuilt via db push, so integration runs alone are not proof that deployment migration SQL is correct; review the migration too. Session cleanup is deliberately limited to used tokens strictly older than the grace window during ordinary successful rotation, never unused sibling tokens.

Repository and DI boundaries
AuthRepositoryModule explains why the auth dynamic submodules require explicitly imported leaf modules (apps/api/src/auth/auth-repository.module.ts:7-17). AuthModule currently imports AuthRepositoryModule at both the outer and NathappAuthModule.forRootAsync levels (apps/api/src/auth/auth.module.ts:101-108) and exports existing services/providers at line 145. Add AuthSessionsModule in both places and re-export that module from AuthModule for auth-passwords. AuthSessionsModule itself exports only AuthSessionService; neither its repository nor AUTH_SESSION_REPOSITORY is public. The spec's memory-module reference is useful for provider/useExisting token binding, but the checked-in MemoryModule actually exports its repository/token (apps/api/src/memory/memory.module.ts:45-46,65-66), contrary to the written private-repository guidance; do not reproduce that export leak. PermissionsModule demonstrates private repository tokens and service-only exports (apps/api/src/permissions/permissions.module.ts:41-61). PrismaRoleBindingRepository demonstrates AbstractPrismaRepository constructor, delegate and domain mapping (apps/api/src/permissions/prisma-role-binding.repository.ts:46-75,108-110); PrismaMemoryItemRepository has the same superclass pattern (apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts:190-201). Auth's legacy repository does not extend that superclass and should not be the template for the new session repository (apps/api/src/auth/prisma-auth.repository.ts:8-21). The root PrismaModule is the package module @nathapp/nestjs-prisma, not a nonexistent local src/prisma/prisma.module.ts; AppModule enables transaction: true and the guarded KodaPrismaClient (apps/api/src/app.module.ts:91-100). Use txManager.run in services and the transaction-aware PrismaService.client only inside repositories; do not thread Prisma transaction clients through public signatures or use raw $transaction.

Rotation and audit risks
US-001's rotate transaction first conditionally updates the active, unexpired session, obtaining serialization on that session row before marking a refresh token used. A zero slide count returns invalid without any token write. A successful unused-token claim inserts the next row and deletes only tokens with usedAt strictly before now minus 30,000 ms. The inclusive >= boundary accepts a token used exactly 30 seconds ago. A competing refresh with a recently used token inserts a sibling next token without deleting unused chains. An older or nonexistent token id on a live session revokes it as reuse and returns reused normally so the revocation commits. Do not throw from the reuse branch and accidentally roll it back; do not reverse the conditional session slide and token mark. A concurrent rotation/logout test is explicitly not requested: the revoked-session invalid predicate and refresh-after-logout 401 anchor the session-row update ordering. Cross-replica/cache consistency is outside scope.
The write coverage guard skips bookkeeping writes (apps/api/src/action-context/audit-coverage.ts:227-245) and throws on successful unaudited counted writes (audit-coverage.ts:287-295); session start and rotation must be wrapped with the two exact new reasons. BOOKKEEPING_REASONS is a typed catalog (apps/api/src/action-context/audit-coverage.reasons.ts:5-40), and its exact key set is pinned by EXPECTED_REASON_IDS (apps/api/src/action-context/audit-coverage.bookkeeping.spec.ts:14,130-134), so update both files. revoke is deliberately not bookkeeping: logout owns an audited transaction. AuditRecorder.audited runs the callback and entries in one transaction, and record explicitly refuses calls outside a transaction (apps/api/src/audit/audit-recorder.service.ts:29-48).
